recall_prompt: Say how you would do this one — name the formula you use and how many common differences you add.

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: State the nth term formula
steps.margin_note: First mark. The examiner looks for a = 3, d = 2 and the formula aₙ = a + (n − 1)d written down before any number is put in.
steps.memory_tip: Count gaps, not terms: n − 1 common differences take you to the nth term.
lines: The sequence 3, 5, 7, 9, … is an A.P. with first term a = 3
For an A.P., the nth term is  aₙ = a + (n − 1)d

recall.must_convey: That a = 3, d = 2 and the nth term formula aₙ = a + (n − 1)d are stated.
accept: first term is three and common difference is two
use the nth term formula a plus n minus one d
write a equals three d equals two then the formula
a three d two, nth term formula rasta
state the arithmetic progression nth term formula

steps.why: The nth term formula turns the words "10th term" into arithmetic. Writing a, d and the formula earns the method mark even if the arithmetic then slips.
common_mistakes: Taking d = 3 − 5 = −2 by subtracting the wrong way round.
Writing aₙ = a + nd, which gives the 11th term instead of the 10th.

steps.label: Substitute n = 10
steps.margin_note: Second mark. 9 × 2 = 18, so the answer is 21. A student who writes 23 has added ten common differences instead of nine.

accept: substitute n equals ten to get three plus nine twos
nine times two is eighteen so the answer is twenty one
the tenth term is twenty one
n ten substitute cheste twenty one vasthundi
three plus eighteen equals twenty one

steps.why: Nine common differences are added to the first term, not ten, and that single count decides whether the answer is 21 or 23.
common_mistakes: Getting 23 by using 10 common differences instead of 9.
